evidence: src/infrastructure/app.ts: createApp(orders: OrderController, stock: StockController) mounts orders.routes(), stock.routes() and errorHandlerMiddleware, so all HTTP setup is in one place
src/infrastructure/error-handler-middleware.ts: STATUS_BY_CODE is the only error-code-to-status mapping in the module
src/infrastructure/in-memory-order-repository.ts and in-memory-product-repository.ts: both are Map-backed implementations of the domain repository interfaces OrderRepository and ProductRepository
src/infrastructure/order-module.ts createOrderController and stock-module.ts createStockController: matching factory functions; server.ts builds controllers only through them
src/infrastructure/server.ts: the composition root, wiring InMemoryOrderRepository, InMemoryProductRepository(seedCatalogue()) and createApp
src/infrastructure/order-controller.ts private guard() vs stock-controller.ts inline /stock handler: minor difference in error forwarding, with no change in behaviour under Express
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The files form one coherent infrastructure adapter module for the order fulfilment API. The HTTP side is handled by OrderController, StockController, errorHandlerMiddleware and createApp. The persistence side is handled by InMemoryOrderRepository and InMemoryProductRepository, which implement the domain repository interfaces. The wiring is done by createOrderController, createStockController, server.ts and seedCatalogue. The module's own building blocks are used consistently: server.ts builds controllers only through their factories, and createApp combines them through routes(). The error-code-to-HTTP-status mapping lives only in error-handler-middleware.ts, and no rule is duplicated across files. One small inconsistency: OrderController wraps its handlers in a private guard() helper that forwards errors to next(), while StockController registers its /stock handler without it. Express 4 sends errors thrown synchronously in a handler to the error middleware anyway, so behaviour doesn't change. This is a minor style difference, not a split, a duplication or a bypass.
